tests.name: mmx-help
tests.stderr:
Send a chat completion (MiniMax Messages API)
Usage: mmx text chat --message <text> [flags]

Options:
  --model <model>          Model ID (default: MiniMax-M3)
  --message <text>         Message text (repeatable, prefix role: to set role)
  --messages-file <path>   JSON file with messages array (use - for stdin)
  --system <text>          System prompt
  --max-tokens <n>         Maximum tokens to generate (default: 4096)
  --temperature <n>        Sampling temperature (0.0, 1.0]
  --top-p <n>              Nucleus sampling threshold
  --stream                 Stream response tokens (default: on in TTY)
  --tool <json-or-path>    Tool definition as JSON or file path (repeatable)

Examples:
  mmx text chat --message "What is MiniMax?"
  mmx text chat --model MiniMax-M3 --system "You are a coding assistant." --message "Write fizzbuzz in Python"
  mmx text chat --message "Hello" --message "assistant:Hi!" --message "How are you?"
  cat conversation.json | mmx text chat --messages-file - --stream
  mmx text chat --message "Hello" --output json

API Reference: https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/text-post

Global flags (--api-key, --output, --quiet, etc.) are always available.
Run mmx --help for the full list.

tests.name: trae-help
tests.stdout:
TRAE CLI

If no subcommand is specified, options will be forwarded to the interactive CLI.

Usage: traecli [OPTIONS] [PROMPT]
       traecli [OPTIONS] <COMMAND> [ARGS]

Commands:
  worktree-apply    Apply isolated workflow changes to the current workspace
  backend           Persist the backend routing (cn or i18n) used by future CLI processes
  dashboard         Browse sessions and agent activity on the shared app-server daemon
  exec              Run TRAE CLI non-interactively [aliases: e]
  review            Run a code review non-interactively
  login             Manage login
  update            Check for and install TRAE CLI updates
  logout            Remove stored authentication credentials
  mcp               Manage external MCP servers for TRAE CLI
  plugin            Manage TRAE CLI plugins
  channel           Set up messaging channels
  acp               Run as an ACP (Agent Client Protocol) server
  app-server        [experimental] Run the app server or related tooling
  remote-control    [experimental] Start a headless app-server with remote control enabled
  completion        Generate shell completion scripts
  sandbox           Run commands within a TRAE CLI-provided sandbox
  debug             Debugging tools
  models            List available models
  apply             Apply the latest diff produced by TRAE CLI as a `git apply` to your local
                    working tree [aliases: a]
  resume            Resume a previous interactive session (picker by default; use --last to continue
                    the most recent)
  fork              Fork a previous interactive session (picker by default; use --last to fork the
                    most recent)
  archive           Archive a saved session by id
  migrate-rollouts  Migrate legacy session rollouts to paginated history
  queue             Queue a text message for an existing session
  delete            Permanently delete a saved session by id
  unarchive         Unarchive a saved session by id
  exec-server       [EXPERIMENTAL] Run the standalone exec-server service
  features          Inspect feature flags
  doctor            Collect local diagnostics for support
  migrate           Migrate legacy traecli (traecli.yaml) configuration to traecli.toml
  help              Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Arguments:
  [PROMPT]
          Optional user prompt to start the session. If stdin is piped, it is appended as a
          `<stdin>` block; without a prompt, stdin becomes the prompt

Options:
  -c, --config <key=value>
          Override a configuration value that would otherwise be loaded from `~/.trae/traecli.toml`.
          Use a dotted path (`foo.bar.baz`) to override nested values. The `value` portion is parsed
          as TOML. If it fails to parse as TOML, the raw string is used as a literal.
          
          Examples: - `-c model="o3"` - `-c 'sandbox_permissions=["disk-full-read-access"]'` - `-c
          shell_environment_policy.inherit=all`

      --enable <FEATURE>
          Enable a feature (repeatable). Equivalent to `-c features.<name>=true`

      --disable <FEATURE>
          Disable a feature (repeatable). Equivalent to `-c features.<name>=false`

      --remote <ADDR>
          Connect the TUI to a remote app server websocket endpoint.
          
          Accepted forms: `ws://host:port` or `wss://host:port`.

      --remote-auth-token-env <ENV_VAR>
          Name of the environment variable containing the bearer token to send to a remote app
          server websocket

  -V, --version
          Print version
          
          [aliases: -v]

      --acp
          Start TRAE CLI as an ACP server over stdio. Equivalent to `traecli acp serve`

      --disabled-tool <TOOL_NAME>
          Disable an ACP compatibility tool for this invocation

  -w, --worktree [<NAME>]
          Start in a fresh git worktree for isolation. Optionally provide a name. Use
          `-w`/`--worktree` for auto-naming or `-w NAME`/`--worktree NAME` to specify. If NAME
          matches a top-level subcommand, use `--worktree=NAME`/`-w=NAME`

      --worktree-base <REF>
          Base ref used when creating a --worktree session, for example `origin/release`

      --worktree-mode <MODE>
          Worktree creation strategy to use with --worktree
          
          [possible values: git, reflink]

      --resume [<SESSION_ID>]
          Resume a local session by ID, or auto-resume the most recent local session if no ID is
          provided

      --session-id <SESSION_ID>
          Legacy compatibility flag for selecting or naming the session

      --shell-tool-timeout <DURATION>
          Hard timeout for shell tool execution. Any shell process is unconditionally killed after
          this duration. Accepts "120s", "2m", or bare milliseconds

      --strict-config
          Error out when traecli.toml contains fields that are not recognized by this version of
          TRAE CLI

      --no-daemon
          Use an embedded server without probing or starting the shared background server

  -i, --image <FILE>...
          Optional image(s) to attach to the initial prompt

  -m, --model <MODEL>
          Model the agent should use

      --oss
          Use open-source provider

      --local-provider <OSS_PROVIDER>
          Specify which local provider to use (lmstudio or ollama). If not specified with --oss,
          will use config default or show selection

  -p, --profile <CONFIG_PROFILE>
          Layer $TRAE_HOME/<name>.traecli.toml on top of the base user config

      --permission-mode <MODE>
          Select the permission mode preset to use

          Possible values:
          - default:            TRAE CLI can read and edit files in the current workspace, and run
            commands. Approval is required to access the internet or edit other files. (Identical to
            Agent mode)
          - bypass_permissions: TRAE CLI can edit files outside this workspace and access the
            internet without asking for approval. Exercise caution when using
          - auto:               Same workspace-write permissions as Workspace Edit, but eligible
            on-request approvals are routed through the auto-reviewer subagent

  -s, --sandbox <SANDBOX_MODE>
          Select the sandbox policy to use when executing model-generated shell commands
          
          [possible values: read-only, workspace-write, danger-full-access]

  -y, --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox
          Skip all confirmation prompts and execute commands without sandboxing. EXTREMELY
          DANGEROUS. Intended solely for running in environments that are externally sandboxed

      --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust
          Run enabled hooks without requiring persisted hook trust for this invocation. DANGEROUS.
          Intended only for automation that already vets hook sources

  -C, --cd <DIR>
          Tell the agent to use the specified directory as its working root

      --add-dir <DIR>
          Additional directories that should be writable alongside the primary workspace

  -a, --ask-for-approval <APPROVAL_POLICY>
          Configure when the model requires human approval before executing a command

          Possible values:
          - on-failure: DEPRECATED: Run all commands without asking for user approval. Only asks for
            approval if a command fails to execute, in which case it will escalate to the user to
            ask for un-sandboxed execution. Prefer `on-request` for interactive runs or `never` for
            non-interactive runs
          - on-request: The model decides when to ask the user for approval
          - never:      Never ask for user approval Execution failures are immediately returned to
            the model

      --search
          Enable live web search. When enabled, the native Responses `web_search` tool is available
          to the model (no per‑call approval)

      --no-alt-screen
          Disable alternate screen mode
          
          Runs the TUI in inline mode, preserving terminal scrollback history.

      --allowed-tool <TOOL>
          Allow a Bash(pattern) command for this session (can be specified multiple times)

      --disallowed-tool <TOOL>
          Disallow a tool for this session (can be specified multiple times)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
